newsitem.title: CONGO: U.S. group ATN Inc to run Congo's phone network.
newsitem.headline: U.S. group ATN Inc to run Congo's phone network.

text.p: U.S. telecommunications group Atlantic Tele-Network Inc (ATN) has won the bid to take over Congo's telephone network with its offer of $42.5 million, the Congolese privatisation committee said on Wednesday.

ATN also agreed to invest about $120 million over the first three years and to keep the 1,032 telecommunications staff of the Central African country's PTT department, committee president Gaston Ange Mabial Ngoulou told state radio.
ATN would take over the network as soon as parliament passes a new telecommunications law, he added.
ATN is a telecommunications holding company providing local and long-distance telephone services in the U.S. Virgin Islands and the Republic of Guyana.
It outbid two rivals for the Congo deal -- France Cable Radio, a subsidiary of state-owned France Telecom and a U.S.-Togolese group African Telecommunications Network.
France Cable Radio is favourite to clinch a much larger deal for the running of Ivory Coast's phone network, CITELCOM.
Congo is one of several African states who are reforming their economies and see privatisation of the telecommunications sector as a catalyst to growth.
It has 0.84 telephones per 100 people. A private cellular network has been in operation for sometime.
